summary: Local LLM server for Apple Silicon Macs with continuous batching and a RAM-plus-SSD cache, run from the menu bar.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: oMLX is an LLM inference server for Macs with Apple Silicon, built on MLX. It serves LLMs, vision-language models, embedding models and rerankers through OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs at localhost:8000. Its KV cache spans a hot RAM tier and a cold SSD tier, so past context can be reused across requests and even after a restart, which helps with long coding sessions in tools like Claude Code. It handles concurrent requests with continuous batching, can serve several models with per-model settings, and is managed from a menu bar app with an admin dashboard and built-in chat.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running local LLMs for real coding work is slow when long contexts are recomputed each time. oMLX caches context on SSD and manages models from the menu bar.
whoFor: Developers pointing Claude Code or other tools at local models
People serving several models on one Mac
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it for a Mac-native local LLM server with persistent context caching and drop-in OpenAI and Anthropic APIs.
requirements: Full Xcode only if you build the native custom kernels yourself

overview: Download the .dmg from Releases and drag it to Applications; it auto-updates and includes precompiled kernels. Homebrew and source installs are also available.
Launch it and the Welcome screen walks you through choosing a model folder, starting the server and downloading a first model.
Connect any OpenAI-compatible client to http://localhost:8000/v1, or use the built-in chat at /admin/chat. Apache-2.0 licensed.

troubleshooting.problem: xcrun: unable to find utility metal
troubleshooting.solution: Building kernels needs full Xcode with the Metal toolchain; use the DMG or make install-no-kernels instead.
GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3 and Qwen3.5 need the native custom kernels; check with native_kernel_status().
